# Named required-check register — FOLLOW-918 (RETRO-263).
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. scripts/gh-pr-checks-verified.sh read two properties of a
# PR's check-run rollup — stability (two identical settled snapshots) and size (a
# completeness floor derived from peer PRs) — and never IDENTITY. So both of these
# exited 0 with "all checks green. Safe to mark READY_FOR_REVIEW":
#
#   1. Six real gates flipped SUCCESS -> SKIPPED. `SKIPPED` was in the regex's
#      success class, and it also counted toward the completeness floor.
#   2. A 37-run all-SUCCESS rollup containing NONE of this repo's gates. The floor
#      is ceil(second_highest_peer x 40/100) = 37 against a reference of 91, so 59%
#      of the rollup could be absent and the gate still settled.
#
# Every "CI verified, exit 0" before this register proved that the checks WHICH RAN
# were green. It did not prove the right checks ran. This file is the identity
# axis: a name listed here must be PRESENT in the settled rollup, and (unless
# marked `any-state`) every check-run carrying it must be SUCCESS. Absent, SKIPPED
# or NEUTRAL on a registered name is exit 3 — UNDETERMINED, not green, and not a
# red verdict on the PR either (the same class as a truncated rollup: the gate
# could not look, so it renders no verdict).
#
# FORMAT
#   <check name>              must be present, and every run of it must be SUCCESS
#   any-state <check name>    must be present in ANY state
#   # comment / blank line    ignored
#
# `any-state` is for gates whose non-SUCCESS state is the documented norm — the
# pre-existing-red Rule I gate, and prod-touching jobs skipped by design on PRs.
# Registering them anyway means they cannot silently DISAPPEAR, which is the half
# of this defect that has nothing to do with SKIPPED.
#
# HOW THIS LIST WAS DERIVED (reproducible, not hand-picked):
#
#   for pr in $(gh pr list --state merged --limit 5 --json number --jq '.[].number'); do
#     gh pr view "$pr" --json statusCheckRollup \
#       --jq '.statusCheckRollup[] | "\(.state // .conclusion)\t\(.name // .context)"'
#   done
#
# then: every name present in ALL 5 sampled PRs, split by whether it was SUCCESS in
# all of them. Sample taken 2026-08-09 against PRs #699-#703 (HEAD f80f41b7).
#
# WHY A FIVE-PR WINDOW AND NOT A LONGER ONE. A twelve-PR window drops any gate
# younger than twelve merges — it excluded `Modal local-source gate (FOLLOW-900)`,
# one of the six RETRO-263 actually flipped to SKIPPED, purely because PR #698
# introduced it. A short window registers new gates as soon as they stabilise. The
# cost is an explicit lag: a gate introduced in the last few merges is NOT here
# until it has run five times, so THE PR THAT ADDS A REQUIRED GATE MUST ADD ITS
# NAME HERE IN THE SAME PR. Renaming a check without editing this file is exit 3
# on the next PR, by design — that is the register doing its job.
#
# The two Modal effect-probe entries below are exactly that manual case: PR #700
# introduced them, so they were 4/5 in the sample and are registered by inspection.
# The two consent-text effect-probe entries (FOLLOW-935) are the same case again:
# introduced by the PR that registers them, so they appear in NO sample window and
# are registered by inspection, per the rule three lines above. `Measured-premise
# register (FOLLOW-952)` is the third instance of that same case, and
# `Seed script import check (FOLLOW-1191)` is the fourth.

# ── presence-only ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
any-state Assert validate_schemas ran in the last 26h (prod)
any-state Rule I — wired-or-dead check
any-state Assert intent-engine + llm-gateway containers reach their own logic (prod)
# Presence-only for a structural reason, not a convenience one: the header this asserts lives on
# the PRODUCTION deploy and never on a preview, so the job is guarded to schedule/dispatch/push-main
# and is SKIPPED on every pull request. Green-required would make it exit 3 on each one. Its
# negative control is registered green-required above and DOES run per PR — that is the half a PR
# can honestly gate on. [FOLLOW-935 AC(1)/AC(5)]
any-state Assert consent-text CORS + cache headers on the deployed origin (prod)

# DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED — forgone coverage, stated rather than silent (Rule AS).
#
#   K.3.6 D-1 live-network smoke (fetchIntentWeights → GET /api/intent/config)
#
# It was present and green in all five sampled PRs, so the mechanical derivation picked it up —
# and it produced this register's first false red, on PR #705. It is genuinely CONDITIONAL:
# .github/workflows/intent-weights-live-smoke.yml triggers on `pull_request` only when the base
# is `main`, and on `push` only for `main` and the `qa-engineer/**`, `backend-engineer/**`,
# `sdk-engineer/**` prefixes — three of this repo's nine agent prefixes. So a stacked PR (base =
# another feature branch) and a push on any other agent prefix structurally cannot run it.
#
# A register entry that goes red on a legitimate branch shape teaches people to ignore the gate,
# which costs more than the coverage it buys. The coverage forgone is real and bounded: on a
# normal main-based PR that job DOES run, and nothing here would notice if it silently stopped.
# Re-register it if the workflow's triggers are widened to every agent prefix and every base.
#
#   Seed archetype embeddings (if any NULL)   [.github/workflows/post-migrate-seed.yml]
#
# FOLLOW-1191 / audit finding E-1 asked for this name to be registered — it is the job whose seed
# step failed on every retained run while the workflow reported `success`, hidden by a job-level
# `continue-on-error` that this PR removes. It CANNOT be registered above, in either section:
# `post-migrate-seed.yml` triggers on `push: main` ONLY, so it produces no check-run on a pull
# request at all. Both sections above require PRESENCE in the PR rollup, so either entry would make
# `gh-pr-checks-verified.sh` exit 3 on EVERY PR from here on — the false-red failure mode this
# register's own header warns about, applied to all future work.
#
# What replaces the coverage, so this is a scope statement and not a silence:
#   - PR axis: `Seed script import check (FOLLOW-1191)` above, green-required, no
#     `continue-on-error`, no secrets. It executes both seeders' module graphs, which is exactly the
#     failure class that went unnoticed for ~11 weeks.
#   - main axis: the job itself now goes RED on a genuine seed failure (its soft-skip is scoped to
#     the `if:` on the seed step), and `Archetype embeddings not-NULL check` — registered
#     green-required above — reads the result it wrote and now fails on an empty or wrong-dimension
#     table too.
# Register it here if the workflow ever gains a `pull_request` trigger.

# NOTE ON HISTORICAL PRs. This register describes the set required TODAY, so
# re-running the gate against a PR that predates a gate's introduction exits 3
# and names it as ABSENT. Verified against PR #695 (81 check-runs), which is
# correctly reported as missing six gates introduced by #696-#700. That is the
# register working, not a false red — a verdict on an old rollup was never
# evidence about today's main.
